вести.gloss: to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)

meanings.en: to lead, to guide, to drive
meanings.note: Unidirectional verb of motion. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)', paired with 'повести'.

meanings.en: вести себя: to behave, to conduct oneself
meanings.note: Вы как маленькая себя ведёте = You're behaving like a little girl

examples.trans: You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'owners' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть владелец.

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ё-таки').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.

examples.trans: This is the mayor's visitor log from police evidence.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'book' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Samsonov, here, please, is your book.

examples.trans: The book is new, we just received it.

examples.text: Самсонов, вот, пожалуйста, ваша книга. Это Сунь-цзы, как вы просили.
examples.trans: Samsonov, here, please, is your book. This is Sun Tzu, as you asked.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: + dative of the person. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'отвечать'.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'отвечать'.

examples.text: Прости, я должен ответить. Да, Аллочка!
examples.trans: Sorry, I have to answer this. Yes, Allochka!

meanings.note: intransitive reflexive verb with infinitive or от + genitive

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вышение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'promotion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Или просто попроси у шефа повышения.
examples.trans: Or simply ask the chef for a promotion.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть повышение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always promotion.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вышений'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('raise').

examples.text: Макс, надо у Германа просить повышение зарплаты!
examples.trans: Max, we need to ask German for a salary raise!

examples.text: Парни, да бросьте вы, какое сейчас повышение?
examples.trans: Guys, come on, what raise right now?

meanings.note: Поздравляю! = congratulations!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to congratulate', paired with 'поздравить'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.en: to please, to be to someone's liking
meanings.note: + dative: тебе понравится = you'll like it

examples.trans: Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

examples.text: А придётся! Не бойся, тебе понравится.
examples.trans: Well, you'll have to! Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offer, to suggest', paired with 'предлагать'.

Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offer, to suggest', paired with 'предлагать'.

examples.trans: But you were offered a job.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу. Что, плохая работа?
examples.trans: But you were offered a job. What, is it a bad job?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'обрести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'acquired / bought'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и приобрести вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and acquired on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют приобрести.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to acquired.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овладелец'). Common masculine noun meaning 'co-owner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы предлагаем тебе стать совладельцем ресторана.
examples.trans: We are offering you to become co-owner of the restaurant.
More accurately, the restaurant gained a new co-owner.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').
